title: Vocabulary: resilience and self
keyIdea: Resilience is bouncing back after a setback. A setback is something going wrong that slows you down for now. A trigger is what sets off a big feeling, and distress is a feeling so big you cannot think. To regulate is to bring that feeling down until you can think, not to make it vanish. Self-talk is what you say to yourself in your head. A growth mindset says you can get better with practice; a fixed mindset says you cannot change. To persevere is to keep going, trying new ways.

kid: Things go wrong for everyone. A setback is something going wrong that slows you down for now. It is not the end. Sam does not pass his swimming badge. That is a setback. Resilience means bouncing back after a setback. Resilient people still get upset. They just get back up.

A trigger is the thing that sets off a big feeling. A boy laughs at Sam. That is the trigger. Distress is a feeling so big that you cannot think. To regulate means to bring the feeling down until you can think again. Slow breaths help. So does saying the name of the feeling. The feeling does not have to go to zero.

Self-talk is the words you say to yourself in your head. A fixed mindset says, "I am just bad at this. I cannot change." A growth mindset says, "I cannot do it yet. Practice will help." Growth mindset is not just being cheerful. It means you believe you can get better.

To persevere means to keep going when it is hard. Doing the same thing again and again helps a little. Trying a new way, or asking for help, helps much more. Every setback is a chance to use all these words.
adult: This topic gives children aged 7 to 10 the words for hard moments: resilience, setback, trigger, distress, regulate, self-talk, growth mindset, fixed mindset and persevere. A clear word helps a child notice what is going on. Then they can choose what to do next.

The lab follows one story. Learners drag each word onto the moment it names. They turn a distress meter down with tools that work. They swap fixed thoughts for growth ones. Then they pick a plan each week so Sam can reach his swimming badge after a setback.

Common mistakes: thinking resilience means never getting upset, or that to regulate means to make a feeling vanish or hide it. Many children think growth mindset just means being positive. It means believing you can get better with practice and new ways. Some think to persevere is to repeat the same thing. Children also mix up a trigger, which sets off a feeling, with a setback, which is the thing going wrong.
At home, use the words after real events, and use them about yourself too. Praise the way your child worked, such as trying a new way or asking for help, rather than saying they are clever.

familyTip: After a hard moment, use the words together: what was the setback, what was the trigger, how did you regulate, and what will you try next time? Share one setback of your own too.

practice.prompt: Ella's sandcastle is knocked over by a wave. What is this?
practice.hint: Which word means something going wrong that slows you down for now?
practice.explain: A setback is something going wrong that slows you down. Ella can build it again further up the beach.

practice.prompt: Omar's anger is at {n} out of 10. He breathes out slowly until it drops to 4 and he can think. What did he do?
practice.hint: Which word means bringing a feeling down until you can think?
practice.explain: Bringing the feeling from {n} down to 4, where he can think, is regulating. It did not have to reach zero.

practice.prompt: Which thought shows a growth mindset?
choices: I can't do fractions yet, but practice will help.
Some people just can't do fractions.
practice.hint: Growth mindset is about getting better, not just feeling happy.
practice.explain: Saying you can improve with practice is growth mindset. Being cheerful is not the same thing, and the last one is fixed mindset.

practice.prompt: Lily has missed the netball hoop {n} times. Which plan shows she will persevere wisely?
choices: Try a new way, like bending her knees more
practice.hint: Persevering means keeping going and trying new ways.
practice.explain: After {n} misses, keeping going with a new way gives her the best chance. Trying the same thing again helps much less.

practice.prompt: A dog barks suddenly and Jay's worry shoots up. What is the barking?
practice.hint: Which word means the thing that sets off a big feeling?
practice.explain: The barking set off Jay's worry, so it is the trigger.

pool.hint: Resilient people do still get upset.
pool.explain: Resilience is bouncing back after a setback. You can feel upset and still be resilient.

choices: In his head, Ali says, "Keep going, you can do this."
A teacher reads a story aloud
pool.hint: Self-talk happens inside your own head.
pool.explain: Self-talk is what you say to yourself in your head, like Ali's "Keep going".

pool.prompt: Which thought shows a fixed mindset?
choices: I'll never be good at drawing. I just can't.
Drawing is hard for me now, but I'm learning.
I'll ask how to draw hands better.
pool.hint: A fixed mindset says you cannot change.
pool.explain: "I'll never be good" says you cannot change, which is fixed mindset. The other two show growth.

pool.prompt: Noor is crying so hard she cannot think or speak. What word fits?
pool.hint: Which word names a feeling so big you cannot think?
pool.explain: Distress is a feeling so big that you cannot think. Regulating would be bringing it down.

pool.prompt: Sam's meter is at {n} out of 10. Which tool helps him regulate?
choices: Shout at the person who laughed
Slow breaths with a long breath out
Keep thinking about it again and again
pool.hint: Which one brings the feeling down instead of up?
pool.explain: Slow breaths with a long out-breath calm the body, so the meter falls from {n}. Shouting and going over it again push it up.

pool.prompt: Max tried to learn a song for {n} weeks and kept going, practising a new part each day. Which word fits best?
pool.hint: Which word means keeping going when it is hard?
pool.explain: Keeping going for {n} weeks and trying new parts is persevering.

pool.prompt: Which is the best example of resilience?
choices: Ruby is upset when she loses, then trains and plays again
Ruby says she does not care about losing
pool.hint: Look for falling down and getting back up.
pool.explain: Being upset and then training and playing again is bouncing back: resilience. Avoiding hard things or not caring is not.

pool.prompt: What is the difference between a trigger and a setback?
choices: A trigger sets off a feeling; a setback is something going wrong
A setback is always someone being unkind
pool.hint: One word is about feelings starting; the other is about plans going wrong.
pool.explain: A trigger sets off a big feeling. A setback is something going wrong that slows you down. One event can be both.

visual.caption: Growth mindset or fixed mindset? Ask: does this thought say I can get better?

items: Mistakes show me what to change
I'm just not a maths person
If I were clever it would be easy

lab.caption: Flagship lab: put the resilience words on Sam's story, turn a distress meter down, flip fixed thoughts to growth ones and help Sam bounce back to his badge.
